\subsubsection{Monte Carlo}\label{sss:tiaampab-mc}

Statistical characterisation of the class-AB transimpedance amplifier over process
and mismatch together: 200 samples, at the feedback, load and electrode conditions of
Section~\ref{ss:tiaampab}. The closed-loop transimpedance bench runs at
\SI{37}{\celsius}, the unity-gain, drive and power benches at \SI{25}{\celsius}.
Schematic-level, no extracted parasitics.

Per-channel yield is the fraction of samples inside the specification; a chip carries
four identical channels, so chip yield is the fourth power.

Output offset at zero electrode current has mean \SI{-1.08}{\milli\volt} and
$\sigma = \SI{8.91}{\milli\volt}$, with \SI{48.0}{\percent} of samples inside
\(\pm\SI{5}{\milli\volt}\) and \SI{5.3}{\percent} of four-channel chips
(Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-mc-offset}, Figure~\ref{fig:tiaab-mc-voff}). Phase margin is
\SI{64.7}{\degree} on the worst sample against a \SI{45}{\degree} limit,
\SI{100}{\percent} per channel, and loop gain averages \SI{78.65}{\decibel}
(Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-mc-stability}, Figure~\ref{fig:tiaab-mc-pm}). Closed-loop
bandwidth averages \SI{8.84}{\kilo\hertz} and is above the \SI{1}{\kilo\hertz} floor
on \SI{100}{\percent} of samples (Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-mc-bandwidth}).
Input-referred current noise over \SIrange{0.1}{100}{\hertz} averages
\SI{341}{\pico\ampere} RMS against a \SI{2}{\nano\ampere} budget,
\SI{100}{\percent} per channel (Table~\ref{tab:tiaab-mc-noise},
Figure~\ref{fig:tiaab-mc-inoise}).
